View All News Old Second National Bank Completes Integration of Evergreen Bank Group, Expanding Access and Services for Customers October 20, 2025 AURORA, IL / ACCESS Newswire / October 20, 2025 / Old Second Bancorp, Inc. (Nasdaq:OSBC) ("Old Second") has successfully completed its systems and brand conversion of Bancorp Financial's subsidiary bank, Evergreen Bank Group. This marks the final step in its most recent acquisition and underscores 154 years of continuous growth and unwavering commitment to community centered service. As of today, all former Evergreen Bank Group branches are now operating under the Old Second National Bank name. This milestone marks the full integration of Evergreen's locations into Old Second's systems, products, and service offerings. Customers of the Evergreen branches will now benefit from expanded access to Old Second's comprehensive banking solutions, enhanced digital platforms, and a unified customer experience across all locations. Expanded Access and Enhanced Services Evergreen Bank Group customers can now bank at any of Old Second's 55 locations throughout the Chicagoland area. In addition, customers have full access to Old Second's robust online and mobile banking platforms, providing greater convenience and flexibility in managing their finances. "We're thrilled to welcome Evergreen Bank customers into the Old Second family," said James Eccher, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Old Second. "This integration allows us to deliver even more value through expanded branch access, enhanced digital tools, and the trusted service our customers have relied on for over a century." Old Second remains committed to making this transition smooth and beneficial for all customers. For detailed information about the integration and available services, customers are encouraged to visit oldsecond.com/transition/ebg . About Old Second Bancorp, Inc. Old Second Bancorp, Inc., serves as the bank holding company for its wholly owned subsidiary bank, Old Second National Bank with its headquarters located in Aurora, Illinois. Old Second National Bank provides commercial and retail banking services, as well as a full complement of trust and wealth management services. The Bank has offices located in Cook, DeKalb, DuPage, Kane, Kendall, LaSalle, and Will counties in Illinois. Contact: Bradley S. title: ThredUp Releases 2025 Holiday Report
summary: Report Reveals 40% of Holiday Budgets Will Go to Secondhand Gifts
body_text: OAKLAND, Calif. – October 16, 2025 – ThredUp (Nasdaq: TDUP, LTSE: TDUP), one of the largest online resale platforms for apparel, shoes, and accessories, today released its 2025 Holiday Report . The study, conducted by GlobalData and surveying 2,000 consumers, reveals that despite economic uncertainty, holiday spending remains resilient, with a major shift to circular shopping: consumers plan to dedicate nearly 40% of their total holiday budgets to secondhand gifts, up from the 30% they typically spend on resale in their everyday shopping. "While the macroeconomic picture remains unclear, consumers aren't stopping their holiday traditions—they're just getting more strategic on how they participate. They're seeking the most value, and that path is increasingly through resale,” said James Reinhart, CEO and Cofounder of ThredUp. “This holiday season proves consumers are incredibly financially savvy. Close to half of all shoppers are turning old items into cash they can use for holiday gifts. This circular strategy is becoming a major part of how they fund their holiday spending.” Key Takeaways from ThredUp’s 2025 Holiday Report: Circular Gifting is Driving Holiday Spending. Consumers plan to allocate nearly 40% of their total holiday budgets to secondhand gifts. Over half of shoppers (52%) are more likely to focus on getting more items for less money this year. To maximize value, 51% of shoppers plan to strategically spend by starting to shop earlier. Secondhand is Becoming a Preferred Gift. Nearly 66% of all consumers are open to giving secondhand gifts, a figure that jumps to 80% for Millennials. The top reasons for turning to resale are saving money/better value (62%) and finding unique, one-of-a-kind items (56%). Shoppers Plan to Fund Gifts by Tapping Their Closets. Nearly 47% of respondents plan to or are considering selling their own items (e.g., apparel, electronics, luxury goods) to help pay for gifts. This trend is overwhelmingly common among younger generations: Millennials (70%) and Gen Z (57%) are most likely to embrace this strategy. Apparel, Accessories, and Nostalgia Lead Gifting Categories. The top secondhand categories shoppers are considering buying as gifts this year are: Accessories (e.g., handbags, jewelry, scarves): 40% Women's Apparel (e.g., coats, knits, denim): 36% Vintage items (across apparel, accessories, and home): 31% “Secondhand gifting isn't just about saving money; it's emotional. It allows you to find something truly unique or nostalgic that carries a story, which often means more to someone than a brand-new item,” explains Kristen Brophy, Senior Vice President of Marketing at ThredUp. “Consumers are finding that the best gift doesn't have to be new, it just has to be special.” To access the report and review the data and resale trends shaping the holiday season, download ThredUp’s 2025 Holiday Report here . About ThredUp ThredUp is transforming resale with technology and a mission to inspire the world to think secondhand first, embracing the idea that the past is the future, and the future starts today. By making it easy to buy and sell secondhand, ThredUp has become one of the world's largest online resale platforms for apparel, shoes, and accessories. Sellers love ThredUp because we make it easy to clean out their closets while doing good for the planet. Buyers love shopping value, premium, and luxury brands all in one place, at up to 90% off estimated retail price. Our proprietary digital and operations technology are the foundation for our managed marketplace and consists of distributed processing infrastructure, proprietary software and systems, and data science expertise. With ThredUp’s Resale-as-a-Service, some of the world's leading brands and retailers are leveraging our platform to deliver customizable, scalable resale experiences to their customers. ThredUp has processed over 250 million unique secondhand items from 60,000 brands across 100 categories. By extending the life cycle of clothing, ThredUp is changing the way consumers shop and ushering in a more sustainable future for the fashion industry—a future where the future of fashion feels good.

title: Shuttle MCP Server
summary: How we improved the Shuttle MCP server to make AI agents more reliable, with better error handling and context for seamless deployment workflows
body_text: AI agents are changing how we build software, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is at the heart of this shift. MCP lets AI agents connect with external tools and APIs - kind of like giving your AI assistant hands to actually do things instead of just talking about them. We've updated our Shuttle MCP server, and it's a proper workflow upgrade. Here's what's new. What Does the Shuttle MCP do? # The Shuttle MCP server gives AI agents direct access to Shuttle's platform and documentation. Your AI agent can now: Search through Shuttle documentation to understand how things work, ensuring you have the latest information Deploy projects directly to Shuttle List all your Shuttle projects Get detailed information about specific projects View deployment logs in real-time for debugging Instead of copy-pasting commands and switching between your terminal, documentation, and AI chat, your agent handles the entire workflow. The Problem With the Previous Version # The first version of our MCP server worked well for most users. The tools were functional, AI agents could call them, and they'd return the expected data for common workflows. But we noticed struggles in edge cases. When dealing with unusual deployment configurations or error states, agents would sometimes call the wrong tool or miss required parameters. When something failed in these scenarios, they'd get stuck because error messages didn't provide enough context to self-correct. We realized the problem wasn't the tools themselves as they were powerful enough - it was how we presented them to the agents. In edge cases, agents didn't have enough guidance to understand when or how to use each tool. We'd built powerful functionality but needed to be documented better for AI agents to understand. What's New in This Version # The updated server doesn't add flashy new features - it makes the existing ones actually work the way they should. The Agents now have much higher success rates, and even when things go wrong, they know how to recover and fix issues on their own. We've enhanced how AI agents understand Shuttle. Each MCP tool includes detailed instructions that help agents understand not just what a tool does, but when and how to use it. We've also reworked error handling. When something goes wrong now, the error messages are designed for AI agents - they provide enough context and guidance for the agent to understand what happened and how to fix it. Instead of getting stuck, agents can self-correct and try again with a high chance of success. With this, your AI agent works faster and makes fewer mistakes. It understands deployment workflows and can troubleshoot issues on its own. What We Learned About Building MCP Servers # Building MCP tools isn't just about writing the code that exposes functionality. It's about documentation and context - specifically, documentation written for AI models rather than humans. A powerful tool isn't very efficient if the agent doesn't know when and how to use it. You need to provide condensed, structured context that models can actually parse and understand. Otherwise, you're handing your agent a toolbox without labels on any of the tools leaving the agent to guess what to do with it. This means thinking differently about how you write tool descriptions, parameter explanations, and error messages. Every piece of text needs to be optimized for model comprehension, not human readability. If you're building your own MCP server, spend as much time on how you describe your tools as you do on implementing them. The quality of that documentation directly determines whether AI agents can actually use what you've built. Real-World Benefits # Here's where this gets practical. You can now tell your AI agent "Deploy my Shuttle App" and it handles everything using the Shuttle MCP server: Creates a project for you if you don't have one already Deploys the project to the cloud Handles edge cases Catches and fixes common deployment issues automatically The entire workflow - from project creation to a live deployment - happens through your AI agent. We tested this with Claude Sonnet 4.5 to build a complete Rust API from scratch, you can see the MCP server in action. See the full walkthrough here . Getting Started # Prerequisites # First, you'll need the latest Shuttle CLI. If you don't have it installed: Linux/macOS: curl -sSfL https://www.shuttle.dev/install | bash Windows (PowerShell): iwr https: / / www . shuttle . dev/ install-win | iex If you already have Shuttle installed, upgrade to the latest version: shuttle upgrade Configuring the MCP Server # After installing the CLI, configure the MCP server in your IDE or MCP client. For Cursor, you can add it by clicking the "Add to Cursor" button below. Or add this to your mcp.json : { "mcpServers" : { "Shuttle" : { "command" : "shuttle" , "args" : [ "mcp" , "start" ] } } } For other IDEs and MCP clients, check the configuration guide to learn more. Quick Start # The fastest way to try this is with a Shuttle template. shuttle init --from shuttle-hq/shuttle-examples --subfolder axum/hello-world Connect your AI agent with the MCP server, and tell it to deploy. Your app will be live in minutes. How to Use the Shuttle MCP Server # Here are some practical prompts to test with your AI agent once you have the MCP server configured: Note : If the AI agent tries to execute the prompt directly without using the MCP tools first, make sure to prompt it explicitly to use the Shuttle MCP server. Deployment and Migration: Deploy my app to Shuttle Migrate my Rust app to a Shuttle app Set up a Shuttle Database for me Debugging and Monitoring: Check my production logs and see if we have any issues How many Shuttle projects do I have? Questions and Documentation: How to scale my compute size on Shuttle? How to set up a Shuttle Database? Conclusion # This changes how you code with Shuttle. Your AI agent becomes a proper development partner that understands your entire deployment workflow - it can answer questions about your project configuration, check deployment status, review logs when something breaks, and guide you through scaling decisions. The friction between writing code and shipping it basically disappears. Try it now and see the difference for yourself. Check out our getting started guide to set everything up. Or get started with our most popular template: shuttle init --from shuttle-hq/shuttle-examples --subfolder axum/hello-world Share What You Build With the Shuttle MCP Server Show us your projects and share your experiences with the Shuttle MCP server with the community Join

title: How a Teacher Can Make All the Difference
summary: The right coding teacher for kids can flip 'I don't like coding' into a genuine passion. One good first experience changes everything.
body_text: When a child says they don't like coding, the problem is rarely coding. In most cases, one early experience with the wrong coding teacher set the default, and it stayed there. One better experience can reset it just as quickly. Why the First Coding Class Sets the Default At Strive, we hear a version of this from parents regularly: "Eddie doesn't want to be a programmer. He doesn't like coding." When we ask what happened, the story tends to follow a familiar pattern. Their child took a class somewhere. The teacher delivered the same lesson they use for every student, regardless of age, background, or interest. The content was abstract. There was nothing to build, nothing visible to take away at the end. The child wasn't having fun and left with a firm conclusion: coding is not for me. This mirrors what happens when a child says "I hate maths" after one difficult year, or "geography is my favourite subject" because one teacher made every lesson feel like an adventure. A child's first experience with a subject shapes how they feel about it for years. A bad first class can lose more than one session. In some cases, it closes the door to the subject entirely. What a Good Coding Teacher Actually Does When Eddie joined Strive, his teacher focused on one thing: making the first session worth coming back to. The teacher started by finding out what Eddie was actually interested in, then built the lesson around that. Instead of abstract exercises that could apply to anyone, Eddie was working on something that felt like his. That shift alone changes how a child shows up in a lesson. From there, the teacher guided Eddie to build visual, interactive projects through doing rather than watching a demonstration and copying steps. Within one hour, Eddie had something on screen he could point to and explain. That kind of early, visible result is powerful: it reframes coding from "something I struggle to follow" into "something I can actually make." Throughout the session, the teacher celebrated every small success. Confidence in coding builds through accumulated moments where a child feels genuinely capable, as much as it does from working through difficulty. Eddie left that class feeling good about himself and about coding, and it became his passion. What Changes Is the Teaching, Not the Child At Strive, we've seen children walk in convinced they're "not technical," sit through a single trial class, and walk out asking when the next session is. That shift comes from having a coding teacher for kids who made the subject feel accessible and worth pursuing, often for the first time. How a child is taught matters more than any natural aptitude they arrive with. If your child has written off coding after one bad experience, that experience probably tells you more about the class than about your child. A trial session with a Strive teacher is often all it takes to find out what coding feels like when it's taught well.

title: Media Keys vs. Shortcut Keys: Why Dedicated Controls Level Up Your Gaming Session
summary: Take your gameplay to the next level with Turtle Beach. Learn the difference between media keys vs shortcut keys, and see how gaming keyboard media keys...
body_text: What are Media Keys? (Dedicated controls explained) Gaming keyboard media keys are physical buttons specifically designed to control multimedia functions without requiring key combinations or software intervention. These dedicated keys provide universal compatibility across different applications and games through standardized HID (Human Interface Device) protocols that communicate directly with the operating system. Unlike standard keys that perform different functions depending on context, media controls for gaming maintain consistent functionality. They provide intuitive control over playback, volume, and track changes without requiring complex key combinations, making them especially practical during gaming sessions where quick adjustments are essential. Key characteristics of media keys include: Single-press functionality - No modifier keys required Universal compatibility - Work across different applications and games through standardized scan codes Instant response - Direct hardware-to-system communication via HID protocols Visual indicators - Often labeled with recognizable symbols (play, pause, volume) For gamers using Turtle Beach audio setups, dedicated media keys become even more valuable for quickly adjusting game-to-chat audio balance without navigating through system menus or game settings. What are Shortcut Keys? (Customizable key combos) What are shortcut keys in gaming contexts? Shortcut keys are keyboard combinations that expedite common operations by reducing input sequences to a few keystrokes. They typically require users to press and hold modifier keys (like Ctrl, Alt, Shift) simultaneously with regular keys, or use sequential key presses for complex commands. Gaming productivity keys through shortcuts offer remarkable flexibility for both in-game actions and system management. Competitive gamers often customize their key bindings to increase performance via faster reaction times, with shortcut keys serving as programmable macro functions for complex sequences. Essential shortcut key characteristics: Customizable combinations - Players can bind specific functions to key sequences Context-sensitive - Different meanings across applications and games Sequential or simultaneous - Can require multiple keystrokes in specific orders Programmable macros - Advanced shortcuts can execute complex command sequences Modern gaming peripherals like Turtle Beach keyboards integrate shortcut key functionality through programmable buttons, allowing gamers to create custom command sequences for different game genres and competitive scenarios. Media Keys vs. Shortcut Keys: Core differences The fundamental distinction between media keys and shortcut keys lies in their approach to user interaction and system integration. Media keys provide dedicated, single-press functionality that works universally across applications, while shortcut keys rely on key combinations that can vary between different software environments. Speed and Response Time Dedicated keys vs shortcuts comparison reveals significant performance differences: Media Keys Advantages: Instant activation - Single button press with average response times of 1-6ms No memorization required - Visual symbols indicate function Universal consistency - Same behavior across all applications Gaming focus maintenance - No need to Alt+Tab or interrupt gameplay Shortcut Keys Advantages: Infinite customization - Any key combination can be programmed Context awareness - Different functions per application or game Space efficiency - Multiple functions from fewer physical keys Advanced macros - Complex sequences and conditional commands System Integration and Polling Rates Media keys use standardized scan codes that work directly with the operating system at the hardware level, while shortcut keys depend on application-specific programming. At 1000Hz polling rates, media keys can achieve 0.5ms average response delay, compared to software-dependent shortcuts that may introduce additional processing overhead. Why Media Keys Enhance Gaming Sessions Media keys’ benefits for gamers extend far beyond simple convenience. Professional gamers and content creators rely on media keys for real-time audio adjustments, particularly when switching between different audio sources like game sound, voice chat, streaming music, and background applications. Competitive Gaming Advantages Best keyboards with media keys provide measurable competitive benefits: Instant Audio Control : Media volume varies wildly between games, YouTube content, Spotify, and voice chat applications. Dedicated volume controls allow immediate adjustment without breaking focus or losing crucial game audio cues. Communication Management : During team-based games, players frequently need to mute microphones or adjust chat volume balance. Media keys enable these changes without accessing system menus or game interfaces. Streaming Integration : Content creators using streaming setups benefit from dedicated media controls for managing multiple audio sources, background music, and notification sounds during live broadcasts. N-Key Rollover Performance Mechanical keyboards with dedicated media keys often feature N-key rollover (NKRO), allowing unlimited simultaneous key presses to register correctly. This capability proves essential for complex gaming scenarios requiring multiple simultaneous inputs, compared to membrane keyboards typically limited to 2-6 key rollover. Limitations of Shortcut Keys in Gaming Shortcut keys in gaming performance face several inherent challenges that can impact competitive play. The primary limitation is cognitive load - shortcut keys require memorization of different key combinations for different applications, and failure to remember combinations forces users to interrupt their workflow. Response Time Impact While shortcut keys offer customization, they introduce mechanical delay through multiple simultaneous key presses. Sequential shortcuts are particularly problematic, requiring users to press and release a prefix key followed by additional keystrokes, creating an opportunity for input errors during fast-paced gaming. Software Dependencies Shortcut keys often rely on macro software or application-specific programming, creating potential failure points. Tournament environments or restrictive gaming setups may prohibit third-party macro software, limiting shortcut key functionality when needed most. Ideal Use Cases: When to use each type Understanding optimal scenarios for media keys versus shortcut keys helps gamers build more effective control schemes tailored to their specific gaming styles and competitive requirements. Media Keys Excel In: Real-time Gaming Sessions : Media keys shine during active gameplay, where immediate audio adjustments are critical. Volume changes, mute toggles, and playback control work instantly without disrupting game focus. Content Creation : Streamers and content creators benefit from dedicated media controls for managing background music, notification sounds, and multi-source audio mixing during live broadcasts. Competitive Gaming : Tournament settings where software restrictions apply favor hardware-based media keys over software-dependent shortcuts. Shortcut Keys Excel In: MMO and Strategy Gaming : Complex games benefit from extensive shortcut customization, allowing players to bind dozens of abilities and commands to specific key combinations. Professional Gaming : Esports professionals often develop highly personalized shortcut schemes optimized for specific games, using advanced macro capabilities for frame-perfect combinations. Space-Constrained Setups : Compact gaming keyboards maximize functionality through layered shortcut systems when physical space prevents dedicated media keys. Choosing the Right Gaming Keyboard Selecting between gaming keyboard media keys and shortcut-focused designs requires evaluating your gaming priorities, space constraints, and usage patterns. The decision impacts the daily gaming experience more significantly than most peripheral choices. Assessment Framework Primary Gaming Genre : Fast-paced competitive games (FPS, battle royale, racing) favor dedicated media keys for instant audio control, while strategy games and MMOs benefit more from extensive shortcut customization options. Content Creation Needs : Streamers require dedicated media controls for real-time broadcast management, making keyboards with prominent volume wheels and media buttons essential. Turtle Beach Solutions The Vulcan II Max exemplifies optimal media key integration , featuring dedicated volume controls alongside full customization capabilities through Turtle Beach's software ecosystem. For specialized gaming applications, Turtle Beach's peripheral lineup addresses specific needs: Compact Gaming : Vulcan II Mini provides essential media controls in space-efficient designs Wireless Precision : Vulcan II Mini Air offers lag-free wireless connectivity with integrated media functions Controller Integration : The Stealth Ultra Controller provides programmable buttons for custom shortcut combinations Conclusion: Complementary roles of both Media keys and shortcut keys serve complementary rather than competing roles in optimal gaming setups. The most effective gaming keyboards combine dedicated media controls for instant, universal functions with programmable shortcut capabilities for game-specific optimization. Professional gamers recognize that different scenarios demand different approaches. Media keys provide the foundation for reliable, instant control during active gameplay, while shortcut keys enable advanced customization for competitive advantage and workflow optimization. Modern gaming peripherals from Turtle Beach demonstrate this complementary approach, integrating dedicated media functions with extensive customization options. Whether you're coordinating team strategies, executing precise maneuvers, or managing complex audio setups during competitive play, the combination of immediate media control and flexible shortcut customization creates the optimal gaming experience. The choice isn't media keys vs shortcut keys – it's leveraging both technologies strategically to create a gaming setup that responds instantly when needed while adapting perfectly to your unique competitive requirements. FAQ What is the difference between media keys and shortcut keys? Media keys are dedicated physical buttons that control multimedia functions (volume, play/pause) with single presses, while shortcut keys use customizable key combinations (like Ctrl+Alt+key) to perform various commands. Media keys work universally across applications, while shortcuts are context-specific and programmable. Turtle Beach keyboards integrate both approaches for maximum flexibility. Are media keys necessary for gaming? While not strictly necessary, media keys significantly enhance the gaming experience by providing instant audio control without interrupting gameplay. They're particularly valuable for competitive gaming, content creation, and when using advanced audio setups like Turtle Beach headsets that require frequent audio balance adjustments. Can shortcut keys replace media keys? Shortcut keys can replicate media functions but require key combinations and memorization, making them slower during active gameplay. They excel at custom game commands but lack the instant accessibility of dedicated media keys. Premium Turtle Beach controllers offer programmable buttons that bridge this gap. Which keyboards have the best media keys for gaming? Gaming keyboards with dedicated volume wheels, prominent media buttons, and strategic placement excel for gaming. The Vulcan II Max features optimally positioned media controls that don't interfere with standard gaming key clusters. Do media keys improve multitasking during gameplay? Yes, media keys excel in multitasking scenarios by providing consistent audio control across games, voice chat, streaming applications, and background music without requiring application-specific commands or interrupting gaming focus. This proves especially valuable when using comprehensive Turtle Beach audio systems .

title: Ansa Is Proud to Support iGEM Teams. Check Out These Amazing Projects!
summary: When MIT scientists Drew Endy, Tom Knight, and Randy Rettberg held a month-long biological engineering program back in 2003, they probably never imagined that it would pave the way for the iGEM annual synthetic biology competition that has been going strong for more than two decades.
body_text: When MIT scientists Drew Endy, Tom Knight, and Randy Rettberg held a month-long biological engineering program back in 2003, they probably never imagined that it would pave the way for the iGEM annual synthetic biology competition that has been going strong for more than two decades. The iGEM — short for International Genetically Engineered Machines — competition began in 2004 with five teams of students jockeying to develop the most creative synthetic biology systems. Early winners made advances in DNA for information storage and biological photography. Fast-forward to today, and iGEM has snowballed into a worldwide event. Last year’s competition involved nearly 400 teams from 41 countries. Thousands of participants, from high school students to graduate students and their faculty advisors, descended on Paris for the Grand Jamboree where awards were given out. And this year is even bigger. Recent awards have focused on innovations in infectious disease, therapeutic manufacturing to treat depression, and making environmentally sustainable rubber from dandelions. iGEM is more than a global competition. Built on a virtuous circle model, each team contributes new genetic elements designed for the competition to an open source parts registry that all synthetic biologists can then use to accelerate design and experimentation for creating entirely new systems. After 20-plus years of iGEM competitions, the registry now holds more than 20,000 distinct parts. This is how iGEM has fueled synthetic biology innovation well beyond its own annual competition. Here at Ansa, we are proud supporters of iGEM and participating teams. This year we are a gold sponsor of the competition, and we also provided high-quality DNA — up to 20 kb of clonal synthetic DNA — to 22 teams. Each team interested in our offer submitted an entry describing their project and why they thought they’d benefit from our unique ability to deliver long or highly complex DNA designs that most vendors reject. We chose teams based on novelty, impact, likelihood of experimental success, and their specific need for long or complex DNA. Here’s a quick look at some of the compelling projects these teams are tackling: At the Faculty of Science of Masaryk University in the Czech Republic, the iGEM Brno team aims to engineer duckweed, the fastest-growing plant in the world, to enable affordable and local production of protein feed for farmers . The UNILA-LatAm team from Brazil’s Universidade Federal da Integração Latino-Americana is focused on infectious disease, with a project designed to block the transmission of dengue virus from mosquitoes. Team Warsaw 2025 from the University of Warsaw is focused on supporting HCC cancer patients by developing a targeted therapy that could provide an alternative to today’s aggressive treatment methods. Team MSP-Maastricht from Maastricht University in the Netherlands plans to improve efficiency of HVAC cooling systems by coating heat-conducting materials in engineered proteins derived from spider silk. In responses to our question about why long or complex DNA mattered for their projects, teams let us know about the struggles they had faced trying to get the sequences they need for their work. We could feel the frustration! Many teams reported that their sequences had already been rejected by other synthetic DNA vendors due to repetitive regions, high GC content, or strong secondary structures — even after optimization. According to one team’s entry, “Other DNA synthesis companies have either refused to synthesize this construct due to complexity or have failed in synthesis attempts. Through the Ansa platform, the DNA construct has identified as ‘Complex’ yet provides a classification of ‘Guaranteed’ for synthesis.” The Ansa team is excited to have delivered these important DNA sequences to help the young scientists who are taking on some of the world’s biggest challenges. Have a great time at the Paris Jamboree!
